slot_note: Forecasting block seed FC03 (service-parts tail at go-live) re-rooted under the two-layer standard: the seed's withheld-rule shadow-run corpus is capped, so the build keeps the seed's service-parts lifecycle setting and draws a methodological pitfall instead
niche: a distribution utility's protection and control asset team sizing the last-time buy of power-supply modules for an obsolete feeder-protection relay fleet, which must keep every relay running until the relay replacement programme reaches its substation
layer1: an asset-management system migration: work-order history starts at go-live and pre-migration records were not carried over
a work-order export covering every protection asset model, filtered to one model through the asset register
a replacement programme workbook whose approved 2026 plan supersedes the 2025 plan, with deferred schemes
spares held across depots in serviceable, quarantined and at-repair states
substation codes against names, and a 2024 regional reorganisation
stakeholder_role: manager of protection and control asset planning at a local distribution company, who puts the last-time buy to the director of asset management for signature

spine.entity: one work order on one protection and control asset

world.org_type: local electricity distribution company with about 140 distribution substations

driver: A rate is estimated per unit of exposure within bands of an ageing attribute, but the outcome records only begin at a date long after many units entered service, so exposure counted from each unit's entry dilutes the bands those units passed through unrecorded; the forward total, applied to the older band mix the horizon brings, is low by about a sixth.
driver_concrete: Failure rates per relay-year by age band divide work-order failures, which exist only from the January 2021 asset-system migration, by relay-years counted from each relay's 1992 to 2018 installation date, so the 10 to 24 year bands are understated and the last-time buy falls five lots short of the 95 per cent cover the procedure requires.
stump: A competent solver builds the procedure's age-banded failure rates per relay-year in service, counting each relay's years from its installation date, applies them to the relay-months each band will carry until the renewal programme reaches each substation, and orders twelve lots; the step that lands it there is counting exposure before January 2021, when the work-order history it divides into does not exist.

differentiation.task46: task46 measures age on the wrong clock (register age against service exposure rebuilt from a movement log); here age is the plain installation age and is right, and the exposure is wrong only in where it starts: relay-years before the January 2021 work-order migration carry no failure records, a left-truncated observation window, so the shortfall sits in the middle age bands rather than at a step a cohort crosses.

notes: Seed: analytical_tasks/01_forecasting/FC03 (service-parts lifecycle setting only; its shadow-run withheld rule is not used). Forcing event is the OEM's last-time-buy window in its end-of-life notice (a purchase, but the decision is forced by the supplier's discontinuation rather than by a contract or order cycle).
